prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After reading all six first-round statements and the chair's summary, I keep a single-part prize on B045 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The convergence among us is not what persuades me; the reasons are the same as before. The chain from the incretin effect and the physiology of native GLP-1 (Holst), through proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor action and the translational concept (Drucker), to the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) is mechanistically continuous, has been confirmed independently for about three decades, and is now backed by large randomised cardiovascular, renal and weight outcome trials. Maturity is not in question. A single part is sufficient because the achievement is broad and self-contained, and a second part would use a place of the three available on a candidate with a weaker case or a more fragile credit list. I have tested that view against B016, B007, B004 and B035 in the exchange and none of them changed it.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the weak point and I have not found a way to remove it. Habener is not among the credited names, the Mojsov, Habener and Holst priority history is contested and, as far as I can see, nobody on the committee has audited it. Excluding Knudsen leaves the prize one step short of the long-acting analogues that reached most patients, and the citation can only acknowledge this, not repair it. If the primary record shows that Mojsov's contribution to the active peptide cannot be separated from Habener's in a way that favours her, my trio would need to be reconsidered, and the Knudsen option that Wahren-Herlenius and Perlmann describe would become stronger. Finally, a prize for the physiology of a hormone will be read by some as a prize for a commercial product.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius moved from Knudsen toward Mojsov in her round-1 statement, but still finds the exclusion of Knudsen uncomfortable and proposes to handle it in the citation wording, not with a fourth name.
responses.response: I agree with the approach and would like to make it concrete. The citation I propose names the physiology of GLP-1 and the identification of its active form, and states that these established the basis for incretin-based treatment. That wording credits the step from discovery to therapy as a consequence of the discovery, without implying that the analogue design is itself being honoured as a discovery. I would not accept wording that names long-acting analogues, because that would read as a fourth credit. I share your caveat that the early peptide credit has to be checked against the primary papers, and I think that, not the discovery-versus-development principle, is what could still move me to Knudsen.

responses.point: Perlmann ranked B045 third with Knudsen instead of Mojsov because Mojsov's role is disputed, and keeps the unfolded protein response (B007) as his strongest basic-science candidate and an alternative.
responses.response: I have thought again about whether a dispute over priority should lower B045 below B007. I do not think it should, since the dispute concerns one of three names and Holst and Drucker are not in doubt. I also agree with you that the omission of PERK, ATF6 and the work of Ron and Kaufman is a larger problem for B007 than the ballot suggests: a Walter and Mori prize is clean as a pair, but a prize for the unfolded protein response as a whole would be open to the charge of leaving out parts of the response. That, with the still largely preclinical disease relevance, is why B007 stays an alternative for me. On Knudsen I remain where I was; I would take her only if the attribution review shows that Mojsov's claim cannot be defended.

responses.point: The chair proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as his judgment of the discovery core, keeps B016 as the second alternative, and asks whether CAR-T can be defended with June and Sadelain without Rosenberg or Eshhar.
responses.response: I share your framing that this is a judgment and not a settled fact. On the chair's question about B016, I do not think I can defend a prize built on June and Sadelain alone without addressing Eshhar, whose early work on chimeric receptors is outside the credited names, and Rosenberg's adoptive transfer work is real but adjacent. For that reason I would not move B016 into the preferred configuration this year, and I would not argue for it as a second part, but I would keep it as the first alternative because the clinical effect in haematological cancers is large and mature. If B045 stalled over the third name, B016 with June, Sadelain and Rosenberg is the configuration I would then examine first.

responses.point: Sandberg keeps B045 first and proposes holding CAR-T in reserve for a June and Sadelain pair because Rosenberg's work is adjacent, and he treats Mojsov's credit as a judgment call.
responses.response: I agree that Mojsov is a judgment and not a certainty, and your point that high opening agreement does not stand in for an audit of the priority claims is one I accept. Where I differ is on the two-person CAR-T version. A pair would sharpen the gap left by Eshhar and Rosenberg, as the chair also noted, so I would keep the three-name version if B016 ever became a preferred part. I also considered your willingness, and mine in round 1, to pair B045 with B007 as a two-part prize. With a three-person cap, that would mean one person from the B045 trio dropping out or Mori and Walter both being excluded, and I cannot justify either on scientific grounds, so I now prefer the single part.

uncertainties: Priority among Mojsov, Habener and Holst for the active GLP-1 peptide is still unresolved on the evidence supplied to me; this is the one fact that could change my third name.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that acknowledges the therapeutic consequence without naming the long-acting analogues, and how the minority preferring Knudsen would vote.
Whether the clinical case for B007 will become strong enough to stand beside a clinical-translation prize in a later year; this year I judge it not to be.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. None of the credited names on the shortlisted ballots is a co-author, trainee or collaborator of mine according to my profile. My documented scientific connections (single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, co-authorship with Sandberg and other committee colleagues) involve no credited person, and I request no recusal. Optogenetics (B004), the one field close to neuroscience in my own work, is not in my preferred configuration.
